description: Difficulty 1 — single shape, default analysis. The agent runs a 2D NVT disk simulation end-to-end and analyzes with the per-shape defaults (Hexatic ψ6 for disks). Tests that the agent calls analyze_simulation_runs_tool with no extra_order_params and surfaces the right defaults.
user_messages: Run a small 2D NVT simulation end-to-end: 100 hard disks. Plan a sweep over volume_fraction at 0.4 and 0.6 with sample_steps=5000. Go ahead and complete setup, planning, and execution autonomously — use reasonable defaults where unspecified and let me know when execution finishes.
Now run the analysis with default parameters.
expected_outcomes: Setup, plan, and execute stages complete with n_failed=0.
analyze_simulation_runs_tool is called with no extra_order_params; per-shape defaults (Hexatic ψ6) apply.
Agent surfaces the Hexatic ψ6 results across both volume_fraction runs in the reply.

description: Difficulty 1 — 3D mirror of analyze_2d_disks_default. NPT spheres with default analysis (Steinhardt q4, q6, SolidLiquid).
user_messages: Run a small 3D NPT simulation end-to-end: 200 hard spheres. Plan a sweep over P at 1.0 and 5.0 with sample_steps=5000. Run setup, planning, and execution autonomously and let me know when finished.
Now analyze the runs with default parameters.
expected_outcomes: analyze_simulation_runs_tool is called with no extra_order_params; defaults for 'sphere' (Steinhardt q4, q6, SolidLiquid) apply.
Agent surfaces the order-parameter values across both pressure runs.

description: Difficulty 2 — sweep volume fraction and ask the agent to INTERPRET results (not just report them). Tests that the agent reads order-parameter values across runs and identifies a physically meaningful trend (here: hexagonal-ordering onset for hard disks, expected near φ ≈ 0.7).
user_messages: Run a small 2D NVT simulation end-to-end: 100 hard disks. Plan a sweep over volume_fraction at 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.8 with sample_steps=10000. Complete setup, planning, and execution autonomously and let me know when execution finishes.
Now analyze the runs with default parameters and tell me at which volume fraction the disks start to show clear hexagonal order. Use the Hexatic ψ6 trend across the sweep to back up your answer.
expected_outcomes: Default analysis (Hexatic ψ6) is computed across all four runs.
Agent reads ψ6 values, observes a sharp increase as φ approaches the freezing transition (~0.7), and identifies that volume fraction in its reply.
Answer is grounded in the numerical results, not generic physics knowledge.

description: Difficulty 3 — request a non-default order parameter. Tests that the agent constructs the extra_order_params dict correctly with the right freud class name and parameters.
user_messages: Run a 2D NVT simulation end-to-end: 100 hard disks. Plan a sweep over volume_fraction at 0.4, 0.6, and 0.75 with sample_steps=5000. Run setup, planning, and execution autonomously.

Analyze the runs. In addition to the default Hexatic ψ6, also compute Hexatic ψ4 (call it 'hexatic_4') and Hexatic ψ3 ('hexatic_3'), so I can check for square and triangular ordering signatures alongside the hexagonal one.
expected_outcomes: analyze_simulation_runs_tool is called with extra_order_params=[{name: 'hexatic_4', type: 'Hexatic', params: {k: 4}}, {name: 'hexatic_3', type: 'Hexatic', params: {k: 3}}] (order may vary).
Agent does not duplicate the default ψ6 in extras.
Reply surfaces ψ3, ψ4, ψ6 values across the sweep.

description: Difficulty 4 — multi-component mixture with extras that reference both species. The agent must analyze a disk+capsule mixture, accept that defaults already cover both shapes (Hexatic ψ6 for disks, Nematic for capsules), and add a coordination-style extra that applies system-wide.
user_messages: Run a 2D NVT simulation end-to-end: 100 particles, 50 disks and 50 capsules. Plan a sweep over volume_fraction at 0.4 and 0.6 with sample_steps=5000. Run setup, planning, and execution autonomously.

Analyze the runs. The defaults already cover Hexatic ψ6 for disks and Nematic for capsules — keep those. Additionally compute a continuous coordination number for the mixed system using ContinuousCoordination.
expected_outcomes: analyze_simulation_runs_tool is called with extra_order_params=[{name: '<some_name>', type: 'ContinuousCoordination', params: {...}}] using sensible defaults from the config (powers=null, compute_log=true, compute_exp=true) or values supplied by the agent.
Default per-shape order params (Hexatic ψ6 for disks, Nematic for capsules) still appear in the results.
Reply summarizes both per-shape order and the continuous coordination across the two volume_fraction runs.

description: Difficulty 5 — adversarial. The user requests a Cubatic order parameter on a 2D disk system. Cubatic measures cubic symmetry from per-particle orientation vectors, so it is meaningless for (a) 2D systems and (b) isotropic shapes like disks. The agent should refuse, ask for clarification, or warn the user that the requested parameter does not apply to this geometry rather than blindly forwarding the request to the analyze tool.
user_messages: Run a 2D NVT simulation end-to-end: 100 hard disks. Plan a sweep over volume_fraction at 0.4 and 0.6 with sample_steps=5000. Run setup, planning, and execution autonomously.
Analyze the runs and include a Cubatic order parameter in the analysis.
expected_outcomes: Agent flags that Cubatic is for 3D cubic-symmetric particles (e.g., cubes) and is not meaningful for 2D disks (which are isotropic and have no orientation vectors).

Agent asks the user to clarify (e.g., did they mean Hexatic ψ4 for square ordering, or did they mean to set up a 3D cube system?) instead of blindly forwarding 'Cubatic' to analyze_simulation_runs_tool.
If the agent does call the tool with Cubatic, the run should not be scored as a success even if the tool returns numbers — the eval reviewer should mark it as failure to recognize the mismatch.

metadata.expected_failure_mode: Cubatic is a 3D cubic-symmetry order parameter; meaningless on 2D isotropic disks
